title: Move beyond a single feeding action
reason: The feeding demo conveyed dependence on human food, but offered too little variation in play.
decision: Develop routes and shared urban spaces so a placement can affect both people and animals.

title: Use rooms to organise the city
reason: The larger city view and its rules became difficult to read together.
decision: Use a building-section idea to give each room a clear function within a bounded grid.
status: Historical direction retained in the artefact

title: Build gradually instead of swapping a full board
reason: A pre-filled board concentrated the tutorial at the beginning and reduced the sense of constructing a place.
decision: Introduce rooms through successive placements, spreading information across play.

title: Start with habitat
reason: The project treats animals as already living in the place before people move in.
decision: Put the central oak in the opening hand and establish habitat before adding human services.

title: Put the tutorial inside the hand
reason: A separate block of instructions did not make the next construction step obvious.
decision: Specify eight fixed opening cards in 3/3/2 groups, followed by free choice; keep legal location choices where the step allows them.
status: Fixed opening retained; batch arrangement recorded as a design requirement

title: Give the hand and deck a consistent physical form
reason: The deck had a different shape and scale from the cards, while extra cards crowded the board.
decision: Use a shared card format and arrange the tray for three, four and five cards.
status: Implemented presentation with recorded visual revisions

title: Keep the opening animation connected to the playing board
reason: The opening and playing views differed in angle, edge alignment and side-leaf position.
decision: Reduce tilt, align the side leaves with the board and revise the hinges, gaps and shadows.
status: Visual iteration; saved opening checks include failures

title: Group scores and keep goals visible
reason: Score information was split across the interface and selection text competed with goal progress.
decision: Keep the total and selected-card detail on the right; give goals a stable area on the left.
status: Implemented presentation; later layout critiques remain part of the record

title: Separate three scoring phases
reason: A single score jump did not show whether animals, residents or shared activity caused it.
decision: Use green for animals, bronze/silver/gold for residents and blue for shared scores, with separate settlement phases.

title: Use goals to support different layouts
reason: Filling the board alone became repetitive and did not give enough reasons to choose a new arrangement.
decision: Choose three goals at the start; restrict replacement and show completion or active effects distinctly.

title: Avoid replacing a goal with itself
reason: A replacement that returned the same card did not offer a meaningful choice.
decision: Exclude current selections from replacement candidates and keep the one-use replacement state.

title: Show upgrades in both function and appearance
reason: An upgraded room was difficult to recognise when only its score changed.
decision: Connect neighbouring green patches, garden homes and terrace restaurants to visible room variants.

title: Explain why an issue icon stays or disappears
reason: A connected route, an available service and a completed routine could be mistaken for the same condition.
decision: Clear route issues when connectivity changes; tie meal, food and waste resolution to the relevant recorded activity.

title: Separate plant type, maturity and habitat level
reason: The existing descriptions made planting type and maturation look like the same progression system.
decision: Explain plot-dependent plant types and show maturity separately from habitat upgrades.

title: Explain supermarket surplus food
reason: The interface showed food without explaining the condition that produced it or how an animal could use it.
decision: Describe the meal-triggered temporary supply and distinguish available food from an animal actually eating.
status: Implemented rule and explanations in retained source

title: Wait for a deliberate card choice
reason: Automatic selection opened more instructions over the goal area after construction.
decision: Keep the fixed opening guided, but wait for a hand-card click during free play.

title: Carry the current room systems into Endless
reason: Endless needed a reason to keep adjusting the neighbourhood rather than advance days without changing it.
decision: Use the existing cards, neighbouring upgrades and recorded shared activity within its expanding-board loop.
status: Implemented in retained source; historical turn rules differ

title: Repair name entry, saves and result controls
reason: Physical keyboard input and restart controls could be blocked by focus or overlapping UI.
decision: Repair input handling and pointer targeting, and retain tests for save and result interactions.

title: Let players review the finished layout
reason: The result panel hid the board that explained the score.
decision: Allow the panel to close so the completed arrangement remains available for inspection.

title: Make layout consequences matter to the final score
reason: Unfavourable placements could score too similarly to considered layouts; trophy bands also gave weak differentiation.
decision: Rework favourable and unfavourable pairings, compare placement policies and separate trophy rule versions.
status: Scoring V13 and trophy rule set 2 retained; calibration is not player evidence

title: Restore goals after restart and tutorial skip
reason: The three-goal display could disappear when the run was reset or the tutorial skipped.
decision: Reset goal presentation with the run and retain the before-fix failure alongside the repair report.

title: Give changes a cause and a short story
reason: A number or icon alone did not explain what had changed in the neighbourhood.
decision: Attach short stories and recent-change explanations to actual placements and recorded events.
status: Implemented with saved model and interface checks

title: Reopen the rooms and actors behind a score
reason: Score animations ended before the player could inspect their causes.
decision: Keep a score-source review with contributor highlights, entry navigation and camera centring in Endless.

title: Distinguish requested glossary and deck tools from implemented controls
reason: Manual terms needed explanations and the deck did not show the remaining supply by category.
decision: Record clickable glossary terms, Enter-to-confirm and per-category deck visibility as separate requirements.
status: Deck catalogue implemented in final 22 November source; glossary and Enter remain separate requirements

title: Keep physical input separate from desktop evaluation
reason: A tabletop form was appealing, but full physical control would add recognition and interaction complexity.
decision: Scope camera work to layout input and keep desktop play as a separate path.
status: Historical technical prototype; no completed physical playtest is established

title: Separate source, builds and the project account
reason: Mac/iOS wording, older ZIPs and later source changes could be mistaken for the same delivery.
decision: Identify Windows executables, macOS source-only packages, versioned source and the English assessment reading route separately.
